subject: Re: Multipool coverage and fallback strategy for EU expansion
messages:
From: Lara Voss <lara.voss@stello.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mateo Ruiz <mateo.ruiz@stello.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Multipool coverage and fallback strategy for EU expansion

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to a formal go/no-go for our EU launch (targeting mid-May). Before we sign the reserved capacity commitment we need to lock down a couple of operational items so CS and our SRE can finalize the runbooks: 

- Regional coverage: primary pool in eu-west (FR) + secondary in eu-north (SE) — want confirmation on expected cold-start latency to secondary in the ~100–250 token range.
- Autoscale and soft-bursting: we need explicit burst capacity guarantees and cold-start behavior when tolerating brief latency increases vs failing over.
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP): procurement wants a clear timeline tying provisioning milestones to billing and onboarding checkpoints.

I attached an updated traffic forecast and a draft MAP. Can your team propose a pool-sizing + fallback policy that keeps p95 token latency < 250ms for normal load and describes expected degradation during burst periods? Also please call out any regional regulatory constraints we should be aware of.

Can we target a scoped proposal by EOD tomorrow?

—Lara
Lara Voss
Head of SRE, Stello.ai

Attachments: stello_expected_traffic_v2.csv, MAP-stello-draft.xlsx

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Voss <lara.voss@stello.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 11:35:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Multipool coverage and fallback strategy for EU expansion

Lara —

Thanks for the clear ask and the traffic file, that helps a lot. High-level response below; Monica and Soojin I’m looping in for ops + activation details. We can absolutely turn this into a short-run proposal with explicit guardrails by EOD tomorrow. Summary: 

1) Pool topology (recommended):
   - Primary: eu-west-1 (France) — 6x A100-ish equivalent GPUs in reserved pool for steady-state (targeting stable p95 < 200ms at typical concurrency).
   - Secondary (warm-standby): eu-north-1 (Sweden) — 2x GPUs in warm mode (KV cache retained for pinned models), autoscale-to-4 for burst. Warm-standby reduces cold-starts; full failover triggers re-routing policy.

2) Autoscale & Soft-burst policy (proposal):
   - Normal autoscale: continuous-batching + target utilization 65% (scale increments 1 GPU).
   - Soft-burst band: allow temporary excess up to +40% capacity for 3 minutes without route failover; token-serving latency may increase up to ~350ms p95 in that window (we’ll surface this to you via real-time metrics).
   - Hard failover: if burst lasts > 3m or sustained utilization > 80% for 5m, automatic routing to eu-north full-capacity or to fallback hosted variants (smaller model) depending on your policy.

3) Regulatory / data residency: with Private Dedicated, control plane metadata remains in EU. For Stello’s EU customers we recommend specifying the eu-only routing policy in the contract; otherwise logs may replicate for cross-region debugging.

4) MAP / milestones (draft):
   - Day 0–3: Provision baseline GPUs in eu-west and warm standby in eu-north (dry-run network checks).
   - Day 4–7: Load verification with your test suite + traffic replay.
   - Day 8: Canary cutover + CS acceptance.

I attached a short proposal PDF and a MAP spreadsheet with suggested dates. Monica / Soojin — can you confirm whether the warm-standby approach needs any extra netops steps (VPC peering / route propagation), and whether we can commit to 3m soft-burst window as an operational SLO?

Next: I’ll formalize numbers and expected p95 latency for the concrete token distributions in the CSV and send by EOD.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-multipool-proposal-v1.pdf

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lara Voss <lara.voss@stello.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Multipool coverage and fallback strategy for EU expansion

Looping in ops notes and a couple of practical constraints from implementation. Short bullets: 

- Network: warm-standby will require cross-region VPC peering + a route table to allow health checks and KV-sync. NetOps at Stello will need to open the internal CIDR ranges we share in the onboarding doc.
- KV cache: to get the latency benefit we recommend pinning the main model variant during the first 30 days (reduces memory churn). If Stello plans frequent model swaps we should adjust the warm-standby size.
- Soft-burst commitment: we can operate the 3m soft-burst window as an operational target, but it’s not an SLA-backed creditable guarantee in the reserved contract — we’ll include it as an SLO in the MAP. For an SLA-backed credit, we need additional reserved forensic logging and a 12-week run-in.
- Ops runbook ask: please confirm the list of allowed fallback targets (eu-north full-pool OR hosted small-model fallback). If both are allowed we’ll add A/B routing with weighted drain to avoid oscillation.

I’ll add a short network checklist to the MAP and update the spreadsheet. Marcus — I’ll flag anything that requires platform engineering changes.

—Monica
Senior Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Monica / Soojin —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete topology. Procurement wants the MAP updated to show billing start aligned to Day 4 (post verification) and a one-time onboarding fee called out. Also two small clarifications: 

- Can you quantify the expected p95 range for the token mixes in the CSV (short/medium/long) so we can present to engineering?
- For the warm-standby, what controls will we have for model pinning vs rolling updates? We want to ensure our release cadence (weekly model updates) won’t cause KV thrash.

If you can add the p95 numbers and the MAP billing alignment we’ll aim to sign the SOW by next Monday.

Thanks,
Mateo Ruiz
VP, Platform Engineering, Stello.ai
